subject: Publishable privacy snippets + cross-border transfer language for Hosted API
messages:
From: Samantha Lewis <samantha@columbusanalytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@columbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick: publishable privacy language for Hosted API + transfers

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — our engineers liked the latency profile. Legal is doing a short vendor roundup for our procurement team and asked for a 1-2 sentence public-facing description we can show in the procurement deck and in our security review: specifically around (a) what subprocessors you use for hosted inference (high level), and (b) how cross-border transfers of customer requests are handled.

Can you send a couple of short, public-friendly snippets we can paste? They asked for anything that can go in a slide (plain language) and a separate short line for the vendor list we can show in the appendix. We do not need the full DPA, just publishable language and the current subprocessor snapshot (high-level names).

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement meeting Friday.

Cheers,
Samantha
Samantha Lewis
Director of Engineering, Columbus Analytics
attachments: none

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha@columbusanalytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T12:04:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick: publishable privacy language for Hosted API + transfers

Hi Samantha —

Looping in Kimberly and Laura from Legal/Privacy. Below are three short, public-friendly options (varying tone/length) and an appendix-style bulleted subprocessor snapshot for your slide deck. We attached the same content in a DOCX and a CSV for ease of import.

Publishable snippet (short, slide headline):
• "Redwood Inference processes requests on behalf of customers and uses a limited set of subprocessors (cloud providers and managed services) to deliver and monitor hosted API services. We do not use customer data to train models."

Expanded line (for appendix):
• "Redwood Inference routes API requests through geographically distributed infrastructure and, where needed, transfers data across borders using contractual and technical safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses and approved transfer mechanisms). Subprocessors are engaged under contractual restrictions to only process customer requests as instructed."

Appendix — current high-level subprocessor snapshot (can be shown on an appendix slide):
• Cloud compute: Google Cloud (GCP), AWS (compute clusters)
• Edge networking / CDN: FastEdge Networks
• Observability and logs: LogBolt (managed logging)
• Secrets / KMS: VaultCorp (key management)
• Payment / billing: Stripe (payments)

Notes: these are intentionally high-level (names only) — we did not include vendor roles or detailed data flows in the slide. Kimberly, Laura — please confirm that the wording below is publishable (no DPA/contract verbatim). If you prefer alternative phrasing or stricter language on transfers, flag edits and we will update.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if useful.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: public_privacy_snippets_v1.docx, subprocessor_summary.csv

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Samantha Lewis <samantha@columbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-01-21T08:37:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick: publishable privacy language for Hosted API + transfers

Hi all — quick edits from Legal to keep public copy tight and avoid implying processing beyond request handling:

1) Slide headline (recommended final):
• "Redwood Inference processes API requests on behalf of customers. We do not train models on customer input and do not use customer content to improve models."

2) Transfer line (short):
• "Requests may be routed across regions; Redwood relies on standard contractual safeguards (e.g., SCCs) and internal access controls to protect transferred data."

3) Subprocessor snapshot — please use this exact, abbreviated list in public materials:
• Compute: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
• Networking/CDN: FastEdge Networks
• Logging/Observability: LogBolt (managed service)
• Key management: VaultCorp

We removed Stripe from the appendix — billing vendors are contract-only and not needed in the procurement slide. Also removed the phrase "geographically distributed" (too evocative).

Samantha — these are cleared for publishable procurement materials. If you need a legal sign-off stamp or a DPA excerpt, ask and we can provide a redacted DPA snippet.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lewis <samantha@columbusanalytics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@columbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-01-22T16:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick: publishable privacy language for Hosted API + transfers

Thanks Kim and Tessa — this is perfect and exactly what Procurement needs. We'll show the headline on slide 2 and include the subprocessor list in the appendix.

One small ask: could you also provide a short one-line link or pointer where our legal team can view the live subprocessor list (so they can verify vendor names/regions during vendor checks)? A URL or a statement such as "up-to-date subprocessor list is available in the privacy center" would work.

If you can send that link or a single-sentence pointer, we are good to go.

Cheers,
Samantha
